P1.evidence: The call opened on a scheduling apology and small talk and went straight to the open question — 'I'll turn the fuel over to yourself, Mike. How can we potentially help you?' No setter notes were read back despite this being a KFS-set call; Kim was mentioned only as the person who should have sent the reminder. No frame of any kind was set — not the four parts, not three, none — and therefore no frame agreement. This is weaker than the same rep's opening on the Nick Hartas call the same day, where at least a three-part frame ran.

P2.evidence: Age was asked directly ('And how old are you?' — 27) but height and weight never were. Work was covered properly, including the physical nature of it — 'you're on your feet a lot of the times... it's seasonal'. Health conditions were never asked; the joint problems were volunteered ('I do have joint problems... my shoulders and on my right knee'), though the rep did then probe duration well: 'Have these issues been longstanding, or have they kind of come up recently?' and 'when did you stop playing football?'. Training frequency was never quantified — 'consistent for the past four months' was accepted without asking days per week. Results from current training surfaced obliquely through the 1-10 scale ('I'm there for 30 to 40 minutes max... my heart rate isn't there'). No diet question at all — fasting only came up because the prospect volunteered it during pillar two. No sleep question. No daytime-energy question.

P3.evidence: The potential scale did real work — 'let's use an arbitrary scale, one to ten... where would you put yourself?' then 'Why do you put yourself at five or six instead of like a seven or eight?'. The can't-do-it-now question ran cleanly: 'say if you're at your prime athletically, what would you be more encouraged to kind of pick up? Maybe play football again?'. The ripple-effect bridge ran and was repeated when the prospect asked for it again. Where it stalled was impact on others — the rep probed once ('is the business the main piece in your life? I don't know if you're married, you have kids?'), got 'I'm single, got no kids', and abandoned the thread rather than routing to his brother, nieces, employees or the vineyard plan he later volunteered. The reflect-back was the generic want-or-need question, not 'so this isn't really about the weight, it's about X'.

P4.evidence: P4f was the best-executed move on the call: 'ChatGPT, YouTube, TikTok, Google, information is so out there, especially in 2026. So what's really the rationale in getting outside help from a coach like Trevor, as opposed to kind of going on the journey yourself?' — which produced a genuine self-diagnosis. The rep also asked whether he had used a coach or mentor in business. But he never asked what fitness approaches had been tried, what happened with them, or why they didn't stick; the previous personal trainer was volunteered. The gap the prospect named — time management, and needing guidance so he doesn't move wrong — came out unprompted, so it scores as luck, not as asking.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame whatsoever, the same omission as this rep's other call the same day. The two-year question, the settle question, the 'why not' and the line-in-the-sand never appeared. The nearest move was 'is this ultimately a want or a need or maybe even both?', which invites a label rather than making inaction cost anything. The prospect handed the rep an obvious hook — a knee whose musculature already visibly wasted in two years of inactivity — and it was never turned into a cost of doing nothing.

P6.evidence: The trust scale ran as a substitute for the belief question — '10 is, like, I trust Trevor, trust the plan to actually help me, and one is, I don't need this. Like, candidly, where would you kind of put yourself?' — and correctly ran before price. But it never returned a number. Instead it surfaced live resistance: 'if it's going to be like some sort of just selling a course type thing, like I'm not looking for that at all'. The rep answered it and moved straight into pricing without re-asking for the yes, and the all-in question was never asked at all. The playbook instruction to return to Phase 5 on hesitation was not followed — which matters more here than the outcome suggests, because the yes arrived anyway.

P11.evidence: The steps were described in advance — 'We process the investment. I give you immediate access to the program, the app, the community. And what I also do for you is booking to one-on-one call with Trevor' — and a verbal yes was obtained ('Yeah, let's make you a sale today'). Then the recording ends: 'Okay, so I'm just gonna remove the notetaker firstly.' Nothing after that point is auditable. No payment, no Trevor booking, no agreement email or on-call signature, and no welcome-email, Skool-link or onboarding-questionnaire instruction appears on the recording. Payment method was still unresolved between Klarna, credit card, an in-house split and a possible corporate write-off when recording stopped.

objection_plays.detail: Script gap: a deliverable-authenticity objection with no scripted play. The prospect challenged whether Trevor personally answers or whether it is staff or AI — 'I have a few friends that do coaching, fitness coaching. They use AI, the supplement' — and separately refused to buy anything that is really a course. The rep improvised adequately (personal WhatsApp, contrast with the Skool programme) and it landed, but there is nothing in the playbook for a buyer whose scepticism is about whether the human on the other end is real. Worth writing, because this objection will recur as AI coaching spreads.

Money never became an objection. The prospect priced it himself ('So it's 1K a month. You saved three grand') and moved straight to mechanics. No isolation, financial-picture or open-wallet work was needed and none was attempted, which is correct.

notes: Closed, and the process still has two structural holes: no frame at the top and no consequence frame anywhere, meaning the yes rested on rapport and an already-motivated buyer rather than on manufactured urgency. The bigger coaching point is not adherence at all — the prospect disclosed four joint complaints including pain on overhead pressing, and the rep responded by promising the programme would 'get rid of any limitations or injuries that are existing' without once asking whether a clinician had cleared him.
